Step 3 · New measurement or old record?

Do not count the same reading twice

Use Step1’s hypothetical card reader: H means a starred card, E a lit lamp. This ledger fixes the prior at 1% (it does not inherit the Step1 slider); P(E|H)=90% and P(E|¬H)=9%. New measurement selects a model assumption: readings are conditionally independent both given H and given ¬H. Within either case, knowing previous readings leaves the next lamp probability unchanged. A record number labels its source; it does not prove independence.

Predict, then try: Clear → new lit reading R1 → copy R1. Will the probability rise again? Undo the copy, then add a new lit reading R2. Compare the same curve: about 9.17% → 9.17%, versus 9.17% → 50.25%.

No records yet
+ New measurement: lit (×10)
+ New measurement: unlit (×0.11)
Copy last record (×1)
Undo last
Clear

Empty ledger. Posterior = prior = 1.00%. Add one lit-lamp measurement first.

A copy is the same known reading, not another measurement. It adds no information: multiply odds by 1 and the curve stays flat. A genuinely new, dependent measurement can still add information, but needs probabilities conditional on previous results and H / ¬H; do not reuse ×10 automatically. Conditional independence also differs from independence in the mixed population. The independent product is not a general upper or lower bound.

A lit lamp has likelihood ratio 0.90 / 0.09 = 10; an unlit lamp has 0.10 / 0.91 ≈ 0.11. Multiply odds, not probability, by this ratio. The horizontal axis counts display entries, including copies.
